title: A common mistake: = instead of == with words
idea: Two classic word-comparison bugs: using = (assign) where == (compare) is meant, and forgetting the quotes. Spot and fix them.

options: It uses = (assign) but a comparison needs ==
exercises.explanation: A single = tries to ASSIGN, not compare. Testing equality needs ==, so this is a classic mix-up.
== compares. Now the if correctly tests whether color equals "red".

options: yes has no quotes, so Python looks for a variable named yes instead of the word
exercises.explanation: Without quotes, yes is treated as a variable name, not the text "yes". The literal word needs quotes.
Quotes make it the literal text "yes". Now the comparison is against the word, not a missing variable.

exercises.prompt: Which line correctly checks if name holds the word Sam?
exercises.explanation: Compare with ==, and put the literal word in quotes. Only the first line does both.

exercises.prompt: '=' and '==' mean the same thing inside an if.
exercises.explanation: No - '=' assigns a value; '==' compares. Using '=' where you meant '==' is a very common bug.

exercises.prompt: A program checks if cmd == stop (no quotes) and crashes saying stop is not defined. Why?
options: Without quotes, Python expects a variable called stop, which does not exist
exercises.explanation: The missing quotes turned the word into a variable lookup. Add quotes: cmd == "stop".
== for comparing, quotes around the literal word. The first line is the only correct one.

exercises.prompt: Best habit to avoid these bugs?
options: Read the line aloud: 'is X equal to the word Y?' - that reminds you to use == and quotes
exercises.explanation: Saying the intent out loud separates 'compare' (==) from 'store' (=) and reminds you the word needs quotes.

exercises.prompt: The two word-comparison gotchas to remember:
options: Use == (not =) to compare, and quote the literal word
Use = to compare, drop the quotes
exercises.explanation: == for comparing and quotes around literal text - both must be right or the comparison misbehaves.
